text: uh yeah so the only thing is that all sounds good but to tell you the truth i honestly cant say that it is or isnt what should be done because i honestly can only really validate the pipeline for something like that after seeing what it actually looks like (and this is mainly in regard to the stickers  and a problem that was brought to us before is, is that enough space? the reason i ask is there was a point where we had some serious issues to where basically a size 2-3 brush was like 1/3rd of the  painting space and i couldnt even write out the word test in anything that was legible so thats my main concern
resolution: Validated the density concern with hard numbers + a visual proof the user can judge by eye. Reproduced the remembered incident: at the model painter's 16 texels/m base, a size-3 brush is 18.8cm of wall and a 40cm letter gets 6px — 'test' is unwritable (the req_2465 jagged-TesT era; AA was fixed then, density was not). Rendered the same 3m×2m wall (40cm letters, 15cm tag line, size-3 brush squiggle, brush dots) at 16/32/64/128/256 px/m with a supersampled AA brush at true texel resolution, published as an artifact for review: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/824786a4-0921-480b-9b51-d4df16d47fcb. Verdict offered: 128 px/m is the sticker/graffiti density (2.3cm brush line, 51px letters, 12×6m facade = 4.7MB GPU at rest, disk stays strokes per the paint-program ruling); 256 is 4× memory for nose-to-wall crispness only. No code changed — awaiting the user's eye on the mockups.
